hero.description: Master the Regulating Act of 1773—the first major constitutional step by the British Parliament to regulate the East India Company and establish centralized administration in India (UPSC GS Paper-II: Historical Underpinnings of the Constitution).

timeline.title: Historical Evolution Leading to the Regulating Act
timeline.description: Key developments that compelled the British Parliament to intervene in Company administration.

cards.details: The East India Company emerged as a political power in Bengal after defeating Siraj-ud-Daulah.
The Company gained decisive political supremacy over Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha.
The Mughal Emperor granted Diwani rights to the East India Company, allowing revenue collection.
Financial difficulties, corruption, and administrative chaos prompted parliamentary intervention.
The first parliamentary attempt to regulate East India Company administration in India.
The Supreme Court at Calcutta began functioning under the provisions of the Act.
Clarified jurisdictional disputes between the Supreme Court and Company administration.

items.answer: Warren Hastings under the Regulating Act of 1773.

items.question: Which Act established the Supreme Court at Calcutta?
Who was the first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta?
Why was the Regulating Act passed?
items.answer: To regulate the affairs of the East India Company and reduce corruption and mismanagement.

traps.title: UPSC Civil Services Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Trap 1: Confusing Governor-General of Bengal (1773) with Governor-General of India (1833).
Trap 2: Assuming the Regulating Act ended Company rule. It only regulated Company administration.
Trap 3: Thinking the Supreme Court was established in 1773. The Act provided for it, but it began functioning in 1774.
Trap 4: Confusing the Regulating Act with Pitt's India Act. The latter established the Board of Control in 1784.

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Comprehensive analysis of the Regulating Act of 1773 for UPSC Prelims and Mains.

sections.title: 1. Historical Background
sections.content:
By the early 1770s, the East India Company had transformed itself from a trading organization into a territorial power. Following the Battle of Plassey (1757), Battle of Buxar (1764), and acquisition of Diwani rights (1765), the Company gained immense political and economic influence.

However, corruption, administrative inefficiency, and financial crises became widespread. Company officials amassed private fortunes while governance deteriorated. The British Parliament therefore intervened through the Regulating Act of 1773.

sections.title: 2. Why Was the Regulating Act Passed?
sections.content:
Financial Crisis
  • The Company faced severe financial distress.
  • It sought financial assistance from the British Government.
  • Parliament demanded greater oversight.
Corruption
  • Company officials engaged in bribery and private trade.
  • Administrative abuses became common.
  • Public criticism increased in Britain.

sections.title: 3. Governor-General of Bengal & Executive Council
sections.content:
The Governor of Bengal was redesignated as the Governor-General of Bengal. Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General. He was assisted by a four-member Executive Council, with decisions taken by majority vote.

Because the Governor-General possessed no veto power and decisions were strictly majoritarian, constant deadlocks arose when the majority councillors (Francis, Clavering, and Monson) opposed Hastings' decisions.

sections.title: 4. Executive Council Structure
sections.content:
The Act established a four-member Executive Council to assist the Governor-General.

  • Members enjoyed equal voting rights.
  • Majority decisions were binding.
  • Frequent conflicts emerged between Warren Hastings and Council members.

sections.title: 5. Supreme Court at Calcutta
sections.content:
The Act established a Supreme Court at Fort William, Calcutta in 1774.

Composition
  • One Chief Justice.
  • Three Puisne Judges.
  • Sir Elijah Impey became the first Chief Justice.
Functions
  • Civil jurisdiction.
  • Criminal jurisdiction.
  • Admiralty jurisdiction.
  • Ecclesiastical jurisdiction.

sections.title: 6. Centralisation of Administration
sections.content:
The Presidencies of Bombay and Madras were subordinated to Bengal in matters of war and peace.

  • Reduced administrative fragmentation.
  • Strengthened central authority.
  • Laid the foundation for future constitutional centralisation.

sections.title: 7. Restrictions on Company Officials
sections.content:
• Company servants were prohibited from accepting gifts and bribes.
  • Private trade was restricted.
  • Aimed to curb corruption and misuse of authority.

sections.title: 8. Constitutional Significance
sections.content:
Parliamentary Control
  • First parliamentary intervention in Company administration.
  • Recognized political responsibilities of the Company.
Constitutional Development
  • Foundation of centralized administration.
  • Beginning of constitutional evolution in British India.
  • Introduced a modern judicial institution.

sections.title: 9. Defects of the Act
sections.content:
• Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court was unclear.
  • Frequent conflicts between Executive Council and Governor-General.
  • Conflicts between judiciary and executive.
  • Administrative inefficiencies continued.

sections.title: 10. Act of Settlement, 1781
sections.content:
The defects of the Regulating Act were addressed by the Act of Settlement (1781).

Dimension Regulating Act of 1773 Act of Settlement of 1781
Executive Status Governor-General and Council subject to Supreme Court jurisdiction Exempted Governor-General and Council for actions in official capacity
Revenue Matters Brought under Supreme Court jurisdiction (creating massive conflicts) Completely excluded revenue collection matters from SC jurisdiction
Native Customary Laws Undefined, leading to SC applying English common law arbitrarily Directed Supreme Court to respect personal laws (Hindu/Muslim) of defendants

The Act of Settlement successfully reduced executive-judiciary conflicts, laying a smoother track for colonial administration until Pitt's India Act of 1784.
